solutions.check: 32 entries verified against the grid (lengths, crossings, linked-clue mapping)

clue.text: City's empty, beer's off before 10, but some people are virtually satisfied with that

definitions.text: some people are virtually satisfied with that
definitions.note: a descriptive clause standing for a noun

indicators.note: an empty word has lost its contents, leaving only its two outside letters
something that has gone off is spoiled or out of order, so its letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the first and last letters of the word
the five letters of BEERS jumbled
X is the Roman numeral for ten

explanation.surface: A deserted city with the beer gone sour before ten, yet some folk are content with a virtual substitute.
explanation.walkthrough: '10' is a number, not a cross-reference: it is the Roman X. 'Virtually' in the definition points to online activity.
explanation.definitionFit: Online sexual encounters conducted through computers give some users gratification without any physical contact.

clue.text: Intimidates liberal independent political leaders – a bloomer

indicators.note: the leader of a word is the letter at its front, so only the opening letter is kept

blocks.note: to cow is to intimidate
standard abbreviation for Liberal
standard abbreviation for independent
the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A bully cowing liberal and independent party leaders, who then make a blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A bloomer' looks like slang for a mistake, which suits the political surface; here it is literally something that blooms.
explanation.definitionFit: The cowslip is a yellow spring wildflower, and any flowering plant can jokingly be called something that blooms.

clue.text: Impudence of female underwear and smalls

blocks.note: a bra is a woman's undergarment
joins the two pieces
S is the abbreviation for small, so two smalls are two S's

explanation.surface: The cheek of someone flaunting a bra and knickers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smalls' is British slang for underwear, which fits the surface; in the wordplay it is the plural of S for small.
explanation.definitionFit: Brass, like nerve or cheek, is informal British slang for shameless boldness or effrontery.

clue.text: "Break your butt", putting it coarsely, is not to show reserve

indicators.note: the butt of something is its tail end, so only the final letter survives

blocks.note: a break is a rest
the final letter of the word
the slangy, uneducated form of 'is not'

explanation.surface: Telling someone to work themselves silly is, crudely put, hardly showing reticence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Break your butt' reads as a coarse idiom for working hard, but it splits into a break plus the butt of 'your'. 'Putting it coarsely' turns 'is not' into its slang contraction.
explanation.definitionFit: Restraint and reserve both name the quality of holding back one's feelings and staying self-controlled.

clue.text: What's left of drugs supported by gallery

indicators.note: in a down clue, being supported means sitting on top of what comes beneath

blocks.note: E is ecstasy, so more than one gives ES
the Tate is the famous London art gallery

explanation.surface: The leftover stash of narcotics propped up by an art gallery.
explanation.walkthrough: E for ecstasy is a common crossword abbreviation; the Tate is a group of British art galleries.
explanation.definitionFit: A person's estate is the property and money remaining after death, passed on to heirs.

clue.text: Quite open about one's sexuality, very attractive and firm

blocks.note: someone who is out has declared their sexuality publicly
British slang for good-looking

explanation.surface: A description of someone openly gay, gorgeous and toned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Firm' looks like part of the physical description, a firm body, but it is the definition as a noun: a company. 'Fit' meaning sexy is British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: An outfit is an informal word for a business, organisation or company, just as a firm is.

clue.text: (& 10ac.) 'Hidden drawers' pun is recycled

indicators.note: recycled material is broken down and reformed into something new

blocks.note: the ten letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A joke about concealed knickers is an old one being reused.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drawers' is an old word for underpants, which fits the theme of hidden things; the quote marks are surface dressing.
explanation.definitionFit: Something kept under wraps is concealed or kept secret from public view.

clue.text: Who dreams of a soft drink and sits around?

definitions.note: a clause standing for the noun 'one who dreams'

indicators.note: letters moved around are put in a different order

blocks.note: Fanta is a well-known fizzy orange drink
the four letters jumbled

explanation.surface: A question about a lazy person who lounges about daydreaming of fizzy pop.
explanation.walkthrough: The question form disguises the definition: 'Who dreams' stands for a person who dreams.
explanation.definitionFit: A fantasist is a person given to daydreaming or inventing elaborate imaginary scenarios.

clue.text: Camembert or cheddar, burnt inside

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the run of words, spanning their joins

blocks.note: found across the end of the first word, the second, and the start of the third

explanation.surface: A choice between two cheeses, one of them scorched in the middle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inside' seems to describe where the cheese is burnt; it points to the letters lying inside the cheese names.
explanation.definitionFit: To torch something is to set it on fire, so torched means set alight or scorched.

clue.text: Administrator set about shafting firm

indicators.note: to turn something about is to move it round into a new order
a shaft driven into something goes inside it

blocks.note: the three letters jumbled
firm and true both mean steady and loyal

explanation.surface: A company administrator conspiring to cheat the firm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shafting' reads as slang for cheating, which fits a corrupt administrator; here it means being driven inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A trustee is someone legally appointed to manage property or funds on behalf of others.

clue.text: see 6dn.
One who contributes greatly to the process of Government-awarded contracts?

definitions.text: One who contributes greatly to the process of Government-awarded contracts?

blocks.clueFragment: One who contributes greatly to the process of Government-awarded contracts?
blocks.note: surface reading: a key participant in public procurement
setter's reading: someone who gives large sums of money to the ruling party and is rewarded with deals

explanation.walkthrough: A satirical jab: 'contributes' sounds like doing work on contracts, but means donating money to the governing Conservatives, hinting at cronyism.
explanation.definitionFit: A wealthy backer who gives money to the Conservative Party may, the clue implies, be rewarded with state contracts.

clue.text: Starlet is crap in a final performance

definitions.note: singular phrase for a plural noun

indicators.note: something crap is badly made, so its letters come out in a mess

blocks.note: the nine letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A young actress is awful in her farewell show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Performance' suggests the stage, but the rites are performed by a priest for the dying.
explanation.definitionFit: The last rites are the religious ceremony performed for someone close to death, the final rite they receive.

clue.text: see 23ac.
Having seen better days, the state finally admits boob

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the next word

blocks.note: PA is the postal abbreviation for Pennsylvania
the closing letter of the word
slang for a breast

explanation.surface: A worn-out government at last owning up to a blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Admits' looks like a containment signal, but it simply supplies its last letter. 'Boob' reads as a mistake; here it is the anatomical slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone past it is too old to function well any more, worn out and over the hill.

clue.text: A game one would play, given sun, sex, atmosphere and energy

blocks.note: Sol is the Latin name for the sun
'it' is a coy euphemism for sex
an air is an atmosphere or mood
E is the symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A holiday list of sun, sex and atmosphere, and the game anyone would happily play there.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One would play' hints that the game is played alone, by one person.
explanation.definitionFit: Solitaire is a card or peg game designed to be played by a single person.

clue.text: Sex act with flatulence, which makes progress difficult

definitions.note: a relative clause standing for a noun

blocks.note: slang for oral sex
wind is gas in the gut

explanation.surface: An embarrassing bedroom moment that rather stalls proceedings.
explanation.walkthrough: The crude surface hides a nautical or cycling term for wind blowing against your direction of travel.
explanation.definitionFit: A wind blowing directly against the direction of movement slows a ship, plane or cyclist.

clue.text: Protest about Republican Cathy being gutless – not welcomed by authoritarian leader

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece is wrapped round another
without its guts a word keeps only its outer shell of first and last letters

blocks.note: a demo is a protest march
CA is circa, about
standard abbreviation
the name with its middle removed

explanation.surface: A demonstration about a Republican called Cathy, frowned on by a dictator.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' does double duty in effect: it is CA, the circa abbreviation, which then goes about R.
explanation.definitionFit: Government by the people through elections is exactly what dictators and autocrats oppose and suppress.

clue.text: City needs to repay the debt, having pocketed American capital

indicators.note: putting something in your pocket places it inside
a capital letter is the first one, so only the initial is kept

blocks.note: to settle a debt is to pay it off
the initial letter

explanation.surface: A municipality must clear its debts after embezzling US funds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' looks like money in a financial surface, but it selects the capital letter of 'American'.
explanation.definitionFit: Seattle is the largest city in Washington state in the Pacific Northwest of the USA.

clue.text: Dish, after second shower

indicators.note: coming after places one piece behind the other in the answer

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for second
a platter is a large serving dish

explanation.surface: Doing the washing-up, then taking a quick shower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shower' suggests bathing, but it is a verb: to scatter liquid in drops.
explanation.definitionFit: To splatter is to spray or spatter something with drops of liquid, as a shower does.

clue.text: Drink of spirits and Ben loses head – prune!

indicators.note: losing the head means the front letter is cut off

blocks.note: a short is a small measure of spirits
the name without its first letter

explanation.surface: Ben downs a whisky, passes out, and someone exclaims about a prune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prune' looks like a dried plum; it is the verb meaning to cut back.
explanation.definitionFit: To prune a plant or text is to cut parts away, making it shorter or more compact.

clue.text: Quote Cyclops on return, causing people to throw up

indicators.note: returning means going back the way you came, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: to cite is to quote
the setter is Cyclops, so the setter refers to himself

explanation.surface: The setter boasting that his own words make readers sick when quoted back.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter's pseudonym in the clue means 'me'. A self-deprecating joke: quoting Cyclops makes people vomit.
explanation.definitionFit: An emetic substance induces vomiting, so it makes those who take it bring up stomach contents.

clue.text: A swinger (both ways) Tom makes use of?

definitions.text: A swinger (both ways) Tom makes use of?

blocks.clueFragment: A swinger (both ways) Tom makes use of?
blocks.note: surface reading: a bisexual partner exploited by a man called Tom
setter's reading: a little door hinged to swing in and out, used by a tomcat

explanation.walkthrough: 'Swinger' and 'both ways' suggest sexual slang, and Tom looks like a man's name; a tom is a male cat.
explanation.definitionFit: A small hinged door fitted into a house door lets a pet pass in or out freely.

clue.text: The bloke with rain-affected protrusion of organ

indicators.note: something affected has been changed or disturbed from its normal state

blocks.note: the male pronoun
the four letters jumbled

explanation.surface: A man with a rain-damaged organ pipe sticking out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rain-affected' reads as a single cricket-style adjective; split it, and 'affected' acts on 'rain'.
explanation.definitionFit: A hernia occurs when an internal organ or tissue bulges through a weak spot in muscle.

clue.text: (& 13ac.) Afro cut executed with hoe? That's beyond me

indicators.note: to execute is to carry out or perform, working the letters into a new form

blocks.note: seven letters of the fodder
the remaining three letters

explanation.surface: Someone baffled at the idea of giving an Afro a trim with a garden hoe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut' looks like the anagram signal, but it is part of the letters; 'executed' does the work.
explanation.definitionFit: Something out of reach cannot be attained or grasped, just as something beyond you is unattainable.

clue.text: Having a corporation topping a large killing

indicators.note: in a down clue, topping means sitting above what follows

blocks.note: a corporation is old British slang for a large paunch
taken as written
standard abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A big company at the top of a huge financial killing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Corporation' suggests a company, but is old British slang for a pot belly. 'Topping' also hints at killing, a further decoy.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something that causes death, as in a fatal or killing blow.

clue.text: Time's against king acquiring charm – rather acerbic

indicators.note: to acquire is to take on, so one piece is followed by another gained beside it

blocks.note: T is the standard abbreviation for time
R is rex, the Latin for king
to enchant is to charm

explanation.surface: Time works against a monarch who tries to win people over with a sharp tongue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Against' simply means next to, placing T beside the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Trenchant criticism is incisive and cutting, sharply worded much like acerbic remarks.

clue.text: Took place in a hospital initially about to go under?

indicators.note: one thing in another sits within its walls
initially points to the first letter only

blocks.note: taken as written
something that was, existed or happened
the opening letter

explanation.surface: Something happening in a hospital to a patient who is about to be anaesthetised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go under' suggests anaesthesia in a hospital surface, but here it means sinking; the question mark flags the loose definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something awash is flooded and covered by water, so it may well be close to sinking.

clue.text: Tory leader on trial, unexpectedly admits truth finally – what a sport!

indicators.note: a leader is at the front, so the initial is the letter kept
an unexpected outcome comes out differently from the expected order
to admit is to let in, so one thing goes inside another
finally points to the end of a word, so its closing letter is kept

blocks.note: the opening letter
the seven letters rearranged
the closing letter

explanation.surface: A Conservative leader in the dock surprisingly owns up, and the onlooker cries out at his sporting attitude.
explanation.walkthrough: 'What a sport!' sounds like praise for a good loser, but 'sport' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A triathlon is an endurance athletic contest combining swimming, cycling and running in sequence.

clue.text: To get sick after USA' s right-wing victory is to benefit

indicators.note: the right wing of a word is its right-hand end, its last letter

blocks.note: the rightmost letter
V for victory
to ail is to be ill

explanation.surface: Feeling ill after a conservative win in America is somehow good for you.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Right-wing victory' looks political; it splits into the right end of 'USA' and V for victory.
explanation.definitionFit: To avail is a formal verb meaning to help, be of use or bring advantage.

clue.text: Prick – follower of Cleopatra's?

blocks.note: first meaning: to jab or irritate, as a sharp point does
second meaning: the word completing the name of a famous Egyptian obelisk in London

explanation.walkthrough: Cleopatra's Needle is an ancient Egyptian obelisk on the Thames Embankment in London; the word follows 'Cleopatra's' in that name.
explanation.definitionFit: A needle pricks the skin, and the London monument is called Cleopatra's Needle, so the word comes after her name.

clue.text: Duke gets into shags with cool titled female

indicators.note: getting into something means ending up inside it

blocks.note: slang for sexual encounters
standard abbreviation for duke
hip means fashionable

explanation.surface: An aristocrat sleeps around with a trendy noblewoman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shags' is British slang for sex acts; 'lays' is the equivalent here.
explanation.definitionFit: Ladyship is the form of address and rank for a woman holding a noble title.
